newsitem.title: SPAIN: Futures expiry powers Madrid stocks to new high.
newsitem.headline: Futures expiry powers Madrid stocks to new high.

text.p: Madrid stocks ended at a fresh closing high on Friday in record turnover, powered by trade linked to the expiry of June Ibex futures, dealers said.
The general index rose 7.20 points, 1.24 percent, to 589.72 and the Ibex-35 gained 87.15 points, 1.31 percent, to 6,761.92, a new closing high but off a new intraday high set today
Turnover sets a record at 185.76 billion pesetas.
Dealers see some retracement on Monday, consolidating the 6,750 level, although sentiment continues positive. The General Index is now seen more likely to rise to 600.
"Once the settlement period was over, we could see clear funds coming in, and short term expectations are obviously bullish," said a fund manager.
Some of bigger stocks outpaced the indices. Telefonica rose 70 pesetas to 4,400 and Iberdrola added 45 pesetas to 1,865. Repsol however lagged, rising just 40 pesetas to 6,430.
Tuesday's Bank of Spain auction will be the focus of attention early next week, with the market split on whether or not a fresh rate cut will emerge, according to a Reuters poll.
But many believe stocks will continue climbing regardless as the flow of funds from fixed income instruments continues.
